note: Supervisory and standard-setter guidance on crypto that Casefold links to its transaction typologies and instruments. Summaries are Casefold's own paraphrase, with the section and page of the source; verify: true = to be checked against the source before it is used as a norm.

guidance.title: Virtual Assets Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing
guidance.summary: Red flags drawn from more than 100 cases, grouped by transactions, transaction patterns, anonymity, senders or recipients, source of funds or wealth, and geography. A single indicator is not proof; several together without a business rationale raise suspicion.

guidance.title: Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers
guidance.status: in force; does not reflect the 2025 revision of Recommendation 1
guidance.summary: How the FATF Standards apply to virtual assets and VASPs: definitions, stablecoins, peer-to-peer transfers and unhosted wallets, licensing, the travel rule and counterparty due diligence.

guidance.title: Seventh Targeted Update on Implementation of the FATF Standards on Virtual Assets/VASPs
guidance.summary: Progress and gaps in implementing Recommendation 15; misuse of stablecoins by illicit actors, including DPRK actors and terrorist financiers, has kept increasing since the 2025 update.

guidance.title: Travel Rule Guidelines (EBA/GL/2024/11): information requirements in relation to transfers of funds and certain crypto-assets transfers under Regulation (EU) 2023/1113
guidance.summary: Which information must travel with a crypto-asset transfer, and the steps CASPs and intermediary CASPs take to detect missing or incomplete information and to handle such transfers.

guidance.title: Guidelines amending the ML/TF Risk Factors Guidelines to cover crypto-asset service providers (EBA/GL/2024/01)
guidance.summary: Sector-specific risk factors for CASPs, including the type of crypto-asset, products that hide the user's identity, and transfers to or from self-hosted addresses, decentralised platforms or providers not authorised in the EU.

guidance.title: Sanctiescreening bij (inkomende en uitgaande) cryptotransacties
guidance.summary: Crypto service providers screen counterparties and beneficiaries of incoming and outgoing transfers, not only their clients; measures are risk-based, acting on a hit is a strict obligation; unhosted wallets carry more risk; examples include blockchain analysis before and after the transfer and holding incoming crypto in an omnibus wallet until the counterparty is screened.

guidance.title: Indicators that could point to unusual transactions in crypto service provision
guidance.status: possibly withdrawn: a DNB overview of withdrawn Open Book statements lists this topic
guidance.summary: Objective and subjective indicators for crypto services; a transaction profile per client; knowing the coins served, including contaminated coins. Points to FIU-NL for indicators.
